repositories.brief_summary: Typechecker performance fixes for the js_of_ocaml compile-time blowup landed alongside new native-atomics work and a Hashtbl determinism RFC.
repositories.new_features_summary: Typechecking-performance fixes cut a pathological compile from 10 minutes to 170ms; Dynarray/Iarray stdlib additions landed.
repositories.new_features:
- Typechecking-performance work on the `js_of_ocaml`/Lwt compilation-time blowup continued, with **occurs-check elision** for fresh type variables during instantiation by [Stefan Muenzel](https://github.com/smuenzel) cutting the offending file from 10 minutes to 5 seconds ([#14913](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14913)), and further **type-path equivalence normalization** optimizations by [Gabriel Scherer](https://github.com/gasche) merged via [#14952](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14952) (building on [#14947](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14947) and [#14950](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14950)), bringing the same case down to 170ms ([#14897](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14897)).
- Stdlib additions: `Dynarray.append_iarray` and `Pqueue.of_iarray` by [Nicolás Ojeda Bär](https://github.com/nojb) close a gap for converting immutable arrays without unsafe code ([#14909](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14909), fixes [#14320](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14320)), and `Option.try_value`/`Result.try_value` were added ([#14941](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14941)).
- Fixed a pattern-matching **switch overflow** bug where the integer-overflow guard failed to account for `abs min_int = min_int`, by [Florian Angeletti](https://github.com/Octachron) ([#14890](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14890)).
- Fixed a **memory leak** in the runtime caused by an unbounded internal cache of stacks ([#14940](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14940)).
- Fixed the generated compiler-cloning script used by opam to work inside opam's sandbox on macOS, where an old bash version broke here-document handling, by [David Allsopp](https://github.com/dra27) ([#14923](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14923)).
- `OCAMLTOP_INCLUDE_PATH` is now ignored during the build, preventing environment leakage into build steps ([#14871](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14871), [#14914](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14914)).
- Fixed a docstring typo in `Bigarray.Array2.init` that reversed the description of `dim1`/`dim2`, by [Tristan F.-R.](https://github.com/tristan-f-r) ([#14973](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14973)).
- Added documentation on the ocamllex `-w` command-line argument to the man page ([#14902](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14902), [#14944](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14944)).
repositories.activity_summary: Nine PRs opened covering native atomics, Hashtbl design, and win32/Sys fixes, while typechecker-performance, POWER, and build-system work continued.
repositories.activity:
- Nine PRs opened this week span runtime, typing, and stdlib work: [Zane Hambly](https://github.com/Zaneham) proposed generating native atomic `exchange`/`compare_and_set` instructions across all five backends, replacing C calls with inline assembly on amd64/arm64/riscv/power/s390x ([#14980](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14980)); [Gabriel Scherer](https://github.com/gasche) opened a re-implementation of `Weak.Make` hashsets using open-addressing with linear probing, reporting a 30% speedup on alt-ergo-free ([#14979](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14979)); [314eter](https://github.com/314eter) proposed fixing `with module type` precedence so `=` and `:=` behave consistently, a breaking change for existing uses of the old precedence ([#14978](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14978)); [Romain Beauxis](https://github.com/toots) fixed a win32 select handle leak reported by liquidsoap users ([#14975](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14975)); [Khalid](https://github.com/khalidbelk) proposed `Sys.filepath_exists` as a safer alternative to `Sys.file_exists` ([#14974](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14974)); [Gabriel Scherer](https://github.com/gasche) proposed enabling `-g` by default in the bytecode compiler to close the debugging gap with `ocamlopt` ([#14971](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14971)); [Tim McGilchrist](https://github.com/tmcgilchrist) opened two runtime-events fixes, correcting a `minor_allocated_bytes` unit-conversion bug ([#14969](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14969)) and adding a missing `EV_MINOR_EPHE_CLEAN` constructor that crashed consumers on out-of-range values ([#14966](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14966)); [Xavier Van de Woestyne](https://github.com/xvw) continued the typing-recovery work needed for Merlin ([#14963](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14963)); and [Török Edwin](https://github.com/edwintorok) opened a draft exposing that `Atomic.t` is not a float in the interface to improve code generation ([#14977](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14977), following [#14976](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14976)).
- The **typechecker path-equivalence and occurs-check performance work** triggered by [#14897](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14897) (js_of_ocaml compile-time blowup) was resolved this week through coordinated contributions from [Stefan Muenzel](https://github.com/smuenzel) ([#14900](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14900), [#14913](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14913)) and [Gabriel Scherer](https://github.com/gasche)/[Florian Angeletti](https://github.com/Octachron) ([#14927](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14927), [#14947](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14947), [#14950](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14950), [#14952](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14952)), taking typechecking time on the offending file from 10 minutes to 170ms.
- Ongoing **native atomics** work builds on the earlier fetch-and-add landing ([#14575](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14575)), with [Zane Hambly](https://github.com/Zaneham)'s new `exchange`/`compare_and_set` PR ([#14980](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14980)) discussing a follow-up to unify with [Gabriel Scherer](https://github.com/gasche)'s proposed `compare_and_exchange` ([#14912](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14912)), while [Török Edwin](https://github.com/edwintorok) separately proposes exposing that `Atomic.t` excludes floats for better inlining ([#14977](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14977)).
- Extensive design discussion continued on a **new `Hashtbl` implementation** guaranteeing deterministic iteration order by [Jeannalyse](https://github.com/Jeannalyse) ([#14956](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14956)), with detailed benchmarking trade-offs explored by [Gabriel Scherer](https://github.com/gasche) and [Stefan Muenzel](https://github.com/smuenzel), feeding into the broader RFC ([#14967](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/discussions/14967)) and the older randomized-seeding proposal by [Hannes Mehnert](https://github.com/hannesm) ([#14291](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14291)).
- POWER-architecture support continued with [Tim McGilchrist](https://github.com/tmcgilchrist)'s frame-pointer PR nearing review completion after feedback from [Olivier Nicole](https://github.com/OlivierNicole) and [Zane Hambly](https://github.com/Zaneham) ([#14505](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14505)).
- Build/CI maintenance merged this week: reverting a temporary MSVC warning suppression now that the upstream issue is fixed, by [David Allsopp](https://github.com/dra27) ([#14103](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14103)); disabling the parsetree-compatibility bot on forks ([#14972](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14972)); and a tooling fix for missing trailing output in expect tests, by [Stefan Muenzel](https://github.com/smuenzel) ([#14959](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14959)).
- [David Allsopp](https://github.com/dra27) continued build-system work in progress, including sanitizing environment variables from the build ([#14915](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14915)), switching the required autoconf version to 2.72 ([#14953](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14953)), merging `Dynlink` into a single module ahead of a later refactor ([#14970](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14970)), and trunk-compiler support for `ocaml-system` in opam ([#14354](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14354)).
- [Florian Angeletti](https://github.com/Octachron)'s long-running **structured compiler diagnostics** proposal remained under active review ([#13766](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/13766)), alongside [Alistair](https://github.com/johnyob)'s `type_approx` refactor series ([#14538](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14538), [#14517](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14517)) and labeled-tuple-projection proposal ([#14257](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14257)).
- [shym](https://github.com/shym) continued work supporting relocatable cross compilers ([#14929](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14929)), and nmote validated a fix for `sigaltstack` failures with musl on certain Intel CPUs, confirmed on hardware and reported upstream to musl maintainers ([#14933](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14933)).
- [Samuel Vivien](https://github.com/samsa1)'s proposal to make `unify` return a `result` instead of raising was confirmed ready to merge pending a rebase ([#14425](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14425)).
- [Stefan Muenzel](https://github.com/smuenzel) shared coq-bench numbers showing a `caml_apply` inlining change reducing runtime by up to 25% on function-call-heavy workloads ([#14925](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14925)), and [Gabriel Scherer](https://github.com/gasche) proposed a refactor to consolidate repeated path-compression logic ([#14910](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14910)).
- [Nick Barnes](https://github.com/NickBarnes) posted a proof-of-concept moving systhreads into the runtime, eliminating the largely-fictional separation between the two ([#14965](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14965)).
- Pending stdlib proposals under discussion include [Brian Ward](https://github.com/WardBrian)'s `Result.all`/`Option.all` for collapsing lists of optional/result values ([#14964](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14964)), [Benoit](https://github.com/benjub)'s `Char.Ascii.is_punct` ([#14957](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14957), ultimately recommended for closure by [Daniel Bünzli](https://github.com/dbuenzli)), and [Jeannalyse](https://github.com/Jeannalyse)'s `Dynarray.sort`/`stable_sort` ([#14848](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14848)).
- [Khalid](https://github.com/khalidbelk)'s earlier `Sys.file_exists'` proposal was closed in favor of the stdlib team's `filepath_exists` design, now implemented in [#14974](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14974) ([#14951](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14951)), and [Gabriel Scherer](https://github.com/gasche)'s `Reoptimize ocamlc -g` PR was closed after [Vincent Laviron](https://github.com/lthls) warned it could degrade the bytecode-debugger experience, redirected into [#14971](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14971).
repositories.discussions_summary: Discussions covered relaxing labeled-argument rules and an RFC for deterministic Hashtbl iteration order via insertion-order tracking.
repositories.notable_discussions:
- [Make unlabeled applications fine again?](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/discussions/14968) by [Gabriel Scherer](https://github.com/gasche) revisits whether OCaml's existing (but discouraged since warning 6) support for calling labeled functions unlabeled could ease adding labels to existing APIs without breaking callers, spun out of the `Atomic.compare_and_exchange` labeling debate ([#14912](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14912)).
- [RFC: Hashtbl: remember insertion order to guarantee deterministic iteration](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/discussions/14967) by [Gabriel Scherer](https://github.com/gasche) proposes an internal doubly-linked list to make `Hashtbl` iteration deterministic even with randomized seeding, weighing a roughly 42% memory overhead against enabling hash-flooding protection by default, with alternatives (a new `Hashmap` module, Go-style intentional randomization) surveyed against Python/PHP/Ruby/Java precedent; it directly informs [#14956](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14956) and [#14291](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14291).
repositories.trends_summary: Coordinated typechecker-performance fixes, growing native-atomics coverage, and careful Hashtbl security/determinism trade-offs stood out this week.
repositories.emerging_trends:
- Sustained focus on **typechecker performance pathologies** surfaced by real-world dune-wrapped libraries (js_of_ocaml/Lwt), resolved through a chain of coordinated PRs from multiple contributors within the same week ([#14897](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14897), [#14913](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14913), [#14927](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14927), [#14947](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14947), [#14950](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14950), [#14952](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14952)).
- Growing interest in exposing more **native/inline atomic primitives** at the assembly level rather than through C calls, spanning fetch-and-add (landed earlier), exchange/CAS ([#14980](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14980)), and compare-and-exchange ([#14912](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14912)), each requiring careful cross-architecture fence and memory-model review.
- Multiple concurrent proposals for improving `Hashtbl` security and predictability ([#14291](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14291), [#14956](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14956), [#14967](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/discussions/14967)) show the standard library team weighing performance and memory trade-offs carefully before committing to a default-seeding change.
- Disclosed LLM-assisted contributions are becoming more visible in PR descriptions, for example a bug investigation credited to LLM assistance in [#14975](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14975) and disclosed LLM use per OCaml's AI policy in [#14933](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14933).

repositories.discussions_summary: Contributors debugged a wget/curl option mismatch, a git-fsmonitor socket failure, and revisited the long-standing npm depexts proposal.
repositories.notable_discussions:
- [Nathan Rebours](https://github.com/NathanReb), [Kate](https://github.com/kit-ty-kate), and [Dmitrii Kosarev](https://github.com/Kakadu) traced a bug where opam passed curl-style flags (`--write-out`, `--retry-delay`) to `wget`, eventually finding the root cause was a stray `download-command: "wget"` string left in `~/.opam/config`, possibly introduced by [#5492](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/pull/5492) ([#7055](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/7055))
- [Kate](https://github.com/kit-ty-kate) pointed [Sora Morimoto](https://github.com/smorimoto) to an existing fix ([#6992](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/pull/6992)) for `repository set-url` failing when Git's fsmonitor daemon leaves a socket under `.git`, and asked for confirmation on the latest alpha ([#7054](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/7054))
- [Kate](https://github.com/kit-ty-kate) responded to the long-open RFC on adding npm/pip packages as depexts, citing limited maintainer bandwidth, competing designs like `opam-check-npm-deps`, and unresolved questions about global vs. local installation models ([#5692](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/5692))
- [Kate](https://github.com/kit-ty-kate) transcribed earlier debugging notes on why parallel read/write of internal files fails on Windows (atomic-rename while a file descriptor is still open), without yet identifying a fix ([#6890](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/6890))
- [Olivier Nicole](https://github.com/OlivierNicole) and [Kate](https://github.com/kit-ty-kate) agreed that switch descriptions should default to blank rather than being auto-filled, leading directly to [#7062](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/pull/7062) ([#7061](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/7061))
repositories.trends_summary: Windows-specific compatibility issues and upgrade/first-run UX fixes recurred, alongside renewed depexts work following #6489.
repositories.emerging_trends:

- **Windows-specific** issues remain a recurring pain point, spanning parallel file access ([#6890](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/6890)), a git fsmonitor socket blocking repository copies ([#7054](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/7054)), and CRLF handling during repository updates ([#7065](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/7065))
- Renewed interest in the **depexts** area following the merge of [#6489](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/pull/6489), opening follow-on investigations into faster install checks ([#7060](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/7060)) and broader platform availability search ([#7059](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/7059)), plus a revived RFC for npm/pip depexts ([#5692](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/5692))
- Code-quality alignment with upstream OCaml, seen in the backtrace/exception-hygiene cleanup referencing [ocaml/ocaml#6728](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/6728) ([#7056](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/pull/7056))

repositories.brief_summary: Rudi Grinberg drove a fix- and test-heavy week (jsonrpc-fiber, semantic tokens, completion, rename) plus a new 1.28.0 preview release.
repositories.new_features_summary: Function-param inlay hints now default on, lazy code-action resolution, and semantic-token/completion/rename correctness fixes.
repositories.new_features:
- Function-parameter **inlay hints are now enabled by default** when a client sends no `inlayHints` configuration, fixing a mismatch between the documented and actual default ([#2097](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/2097) fixes [#1371](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/1371), [Rudi Grinberg](https://github.com/rgrinberg)); [emre](https://github.com/dayangac) had opened an equivalent fix independently ([#2013](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/2013)).
- Inline code-action edits (e.g. quickfixes) are now **resolved lazily** for clients that support it instead of being computed eagerly on every request, reducing per-request work ([#1808](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/1808), [Rudi Grinberg](https://github.com/rgrinberg)).
- The `destruct-line` code action now fires on **incomplete inline `match` expressions**, so enumerate-cases can be triggered directly from the `match` keyword ([#1829](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/1829) fixes [#1595](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/1595), [Rudi Grinberg](https://github.com/rgrinberg)).
- **Semantic-token capability negotiation** now checks the client's declared token types/modifiers before advertising them and emits tokens in source order, fixing incorrect highlighting for clients with partial capability support ([#1860](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/1860), [#1978](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/1978), [#1992](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/1992), fixes [#1138](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/1138) and [#1533](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/1533), [Rudi Grinberg](https://github.com/rgrinberg)).
- **Completion** fixes: incorrect identifier suffixes are no longer left behind when applying completions ([#1964](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/1964) fixes [#838](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/838)), dotted operators are preserved in completion prefixes and resolve requests ([#1890](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/1890)), construct-completion edits stay on the request line after Merlin recovery returns a multiline location ([#2034](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/2034)), and synthetic completion items get stable ordering metadata ([#1882](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/1882)) — all [Rudi Grinberg](https://github.com/rgrinberg).
- **Rename** fixes: infix-operator rename placeholders and edits no longer include the surrounding parentheses ([#1966](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/1966) fixes [#1190](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/1190)), multi-file rename edits use each document's current version ([#1958](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/1958)), and duplicate text edits from Merlin recovery are deduplicated ([#2064](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/2064)) — all [Rudi Grinberg](https://github.com/rgrinberg).
- **Signature help** no longer triggers stale popups at expression boundaries, after completed applications, or after the cursor's application ([#1987](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/1987) fixes [#1162](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/1162), [#1982](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/1982), [#1965](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/1965)), and now respects client support for parameter-label offsets ([#2009](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/2009)) — all [Rudi Grinberg](https://github.com/rgrinberg).
- **Dune integration** fixes: Merlin diagnostic ranges are clamped to document bounds ([#2008](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/2008)), Dune diagnostics with an empty primary range (e.g. ml/mli mismatches) fall back to a same-document related location ([#2093](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/2093)), a missing project build-tool executable is now reported as a diagnostic instead of a misleading RPC error ([#1814](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/1814) fixes [#1417](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/1417)), RPC registry polling stays responsive while instances are connected ([#1919](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/1919)), build-progress reporting honors a client's disabled work-done progress ([#2082](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/2082)), malformed promotion commands are rejected ([#2084](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/2084)), and promotion code-action registration/lifecycle bugs are fixed ([#2075](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/2075), [#2076](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/2076), [#2055](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/2055)) — all [Rudi Grinberg](https://github.com/rgrinberg).
- **Code actions**: the inferred-interface action is hidden once the interface already declares everything the implementation exports ([#2096](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/2096) fixes [#347](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/347), [emre](https://github.com/dayangac)), client-requested code-action-kind filters are respected ([#1802](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/1802)), and malformed or out-of-range construct/destruct/refactor-extract/type-enclosing/infer-intf custom requests now return `null`/`InvalidParams` instead of an internal error ([#2047](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/2047), [#2048](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/2048), [#2049](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/2049), [#2050](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/2050), [#2051](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/2051), [Rudi Grinberg](https://github.com/rgrinberg)).
- **Hover and symbols**: empty odoc documentation tables render without raising an internal error ([#2038](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/2038)), and deprecation metadata is preserved in document- and workspace-symbol results ([#2044](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/2044), [#2053](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/2053)) — [Rudi Grinberg](https://github.com/rgrinberg).
- Fixed a **FreeBSD build failure** caused by `statfs(2)` being declared in `<sys/mount.h>` rather than `<sys/statfs.h>` ([#2070](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/2070) fixes [#1069](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/1069), [emre](https://github.com/dayangac)).
- Updated the `hintFunctionParams` config reference default to `true` to match the new enabled-by-default inlay-hints behavior, and recorded the construct-completion range fix in the changelog ([#2066](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/2066), [Rudi Grinberg](https://github.com/rgrinberg)).

repositories.trends_summary: Test-first characterization workflow, Base-utility consolidation, a Unicode correctness sweep, and Dune RPC stabilization.

repositories.new_features_summary: Merlin 5.8.1 fixes load_path races, ppx index staleness, and `document` query bugs, alongside an OCaml 5.6 preview release.
repositories.new_features:
- Fixed **ocaml-index staleness detection** for ppx-preprocessed files: the index now digests the original `.ml` source rather than the generated `.pp.ml` file, so `occurrences` correctly reports staleness when the real source changes ([#2110](https://github.com/ocaml/merlin/issues/2110)) by [Liam Stevenson](https://github.com/liam923)
- Fixed a **load_path invalidation race** where only the first typer instance noticed a directory change; `Load_path.Dir` now tracks a per-directory `file_id` so every server-mode instance detects stale load paths, fixing a bug visible under `ocaml-lsp` with dune watch mode ([#2109](https://github.com/ocaml/merlin/issues/2109))
- Fixed the **`document` query** returning a neighboring variant constructor's or record field's doc comment instead of its own, by correcting `after_only` detection and removing the dead `last_location` comment-association mechanism ([#2092](https://github.com/ocaml/merlin/issues/2092)) by [Liam Stevenson](https://github.com/liam923)
- Published **merlin 5.8.1-505**, bundling the fixes above with earlier occurrences-staleness and `.mli` open-path `locate`/`document` fixes, plus a **5.8.1-506~preview** build with experimental OCaml 5.6 support (https://github.com/ocaml/merlin/releases/tag/v5.8.1-505, https://github.com/ocaml/merlin/releases/tag/v5.8.1-506_preview)
- Added **cram-test tooling** that visualizes selection ranges with `···` markers around included spans, making selection/location regressions easier to catch by eye ([#2107](https://github.com/ocaml/merlin/issues/2107)) by [Paul-Elliot Anglès d'Auriac](https://github.com/panglesd)

repositories.discussions_summary: Root-cause debugging of outline's synthetic eta-expansion bindings and diagnosis of an opam fork causing an OCaml 5.5.0 install failure.
repositories.notable_discussions:
- In [#2106](https://github.com/ocaml/merlin/issues/2106), [Onyeka Obi](https://github.com/MavenRain) traced the outline **selection bug** to the compiler's eta-expansion of optional-argument functions passed to `List.map`, which creates a synthetic `value_binding` with a dummy location that `Outline.summarize` surfaces as a phantom child; after [Ulysse](https://github.com/voodoos) questioned whether synthetic nodes should appear at all, the fix was narrowed to elide only bindings with `Location.none`, preserving genuine ppx-generated (ghost-but-real-location) bindings
- [#2108](https://github.com/ocaml/merlin/issues/2108), a report from [Akhil](https://github.com/akhiltulluri) that `merlin-lib` failed to build on OCaml 5.5.0 with `Unbound value Seq.delay`, was diagnosed by [Kate](https://github.com/kit-ty-kate) as caused by a leftover, unmaintained `dra27/opam-repository#relocatable` fork left configured from earlier benchmarking work (cc [Eduardo Souza](https://github.com/udesou)) rather than a merlin defect
- [#2112](https://github.com/ocaml/merlin/issues/2112), an `Assert_failure` crash in `destruct` on `object method x with|0`, was reported via a cross-linked [ocaml/ocaml-lsp#1991](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/1991) reproduction from [Rudi Grinberg](https://github.com/rgrinberg), with [Xavier Van de Woestyne](https://github.com/xvw) picking it up for the next maintenance pass
- [#2113](https://github.com/ocaml/merlin/issues/2113), opened by [Ulysse](https://github.com/voodoos), documents a duplicated `occurrences` result on a recovered `let rec` binding, cross-referencing [Rudi Grinberg](https://github.com/rgrinberg)'s report in [ocaml/ocaml-lsp#2046](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/2046)

repositories.new_features_summary: New `--include-empty` flag for `dune describe external-lib-deps`, alias-leak fix for multi-alias rules, and RPC reliability fixes.
repositories.new_features:
- Added an `--include-empty` flag to `dune describe external-lib-deps` so libraries with no internal or external dependencies are still listed in the output, closing a gap where such libraries could not be resolved back to their package or source directory by [Nat Karmios](https://github.com/NatKarmios) ([#15585](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/pull/15585), fixes [#15566](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/15566))
- Fixed a **rule/alias** bug where a target-less rule attached to multiple aliases (`(rule (aliases a b) ...)`) leaked unrelated actions and dependencies between those aliases, so building one alias no longer pulls in contributions added only to another alias, by [Nat Karmios](https://github.com/NatKarmios) ([#15581](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/pull/15581), fixes [#15576](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/15576))
- `dune pkg enabled` now queries a running Dune **RPC server** so it observes transient server-side `--pkg enabled`/`--pkg disabled` settings without needing to acquire the build lock, falling back to a local workspace/lockdir check when no server is running, by [Ali Caglayan](https://github.com/Alizter) ([#15589](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/pull/15589), fixes [#15587](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/15587))
- Fixed **RPC registry polling** so it rescans the registry directory whenever its mtime changes instead of skipping scans after the first change, letting clients such as ocaml-lsp that poll before Dune registers reliably discover the new instance, by [Rudi Grinberg](https://github.com/rgrinberg) ([#15634](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/pull/15634), fixes [#15630](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/15630))
- `Fs_io.read_file` now returns Unix errors as a result instead of raising them, making file-read failures consistent for callers, by [Rudi Grinberg](https://github.com/rgrinberg) ([#15641](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/pull/15641))
- Added `Proc.wait` support for waiting on PIDs on **Windows** via the typed process API, extending cross-platform process handling (`Proc.wait Any` remains unsupported on Windows), by [Rudi Grinberg](https://github.com/rgrinberg) ([#15536](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/pull/15536))
- Performance improvement to **module alias generation** using `String_builder`, measured to roughly halve time and allocation for large alias sets (e.g. ~446μs → ~181μs and ~113k → ~45k minor words for 1000 aliases in microbenchmarks), by [Antonio Nuno Monteiro](https://github.com/anmonteiro) ([#15657](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/pull/15657))
- Documentation added on when to add or skip changelog fragments and how to format them, plus scoping the root Markdown-file check to allow scoped `AGENTS.md` files, by [Rudi Grinberg](https://github.com/rgrinberg) ([#15638](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/pull/15638))
- Documentation added requiring regression tests and fixes to be submitted as separate changes and linking changelog instructions for contributors, by [Rudi Grinberg](https://github.com/rgrinberg) ([#15640](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/pull/15640))
- Added a CI workflow that checks for a changelog entry on pull requests, with an opt-out label for changes that don't need one, by [Sudha Parimala](https://github.com/Sudha247) ([#15505](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/pull/15505), fixes [#15460](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/15460))

repositories.discussions_summary: Design debates covered opam archive-mirror modeling, an RPC-lock restriction called out as unwanted agent-authored code, and a trace-stream graph-events proposal.
repositories.notable_discussions:
- On the opam repository archive-mirrors PR, [Rudi Grinberg](https://github.com/rgrinberg) argued the feature's design is inconsistent with the rest of the Dune language and proposed instead allowing a `fetch` to list multiple URLs tried in sequence, so the "archive mirror" concept need not leak into lock directories ([#15615](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/pull/15615))
- On the multi-alias rule fix, [Nat Karmios](https://github.com/NatKarmios) and [Ali Caglayan](https://github.com/Alizter) debated whether `--force`'s existing (already "a bit arbitrary") behavior around anonymous actions and alias-based display names was worth preserving, concluding it was fine to simplify to `(anonymous)` display and revisit `--force` semantics later ([#15581](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/pull/15581))
- On the `dune shell` draft, [Ali Caglayan](https://github.com/Alizter) acknowledged a check preventing RPC usage was "slop" from an AI-agent attempt to forbid an unsupported case, and agreed the correct approach is to acquire the build lock like other commands and fail otherwise, per [Rudi Grinberg](https://github.com/rgrinberg)'s review ([#15597](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/pull/15597))
- [Nat Karmios](https://github.com/NatKarmios) proposed an opt-in `graph` trace category recording rule executions and dependency edges in the existing `_build/trace.csexp` stream, with detailed schema, sizing estimates, and open questions on rule retraction in watch mode; [Rudi Grinberg](https://github.com/rgrinberg) approved proceeding with implementation, flagging only the cost of enabling such events by default ([#15612](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/15612))
- [Allan Blanchard](https://github.com/AllanBlanchard) reported for the Frama-C team that `deps` no longer loads package dependencies transitively as of a recent commit, forcing manual dependency listing; the issue remains open pending a workaround or behavior decision ([#15511](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/15511))

repositories.trends_summary: Continued RPC-coverage expansion, a test-first workflow for landing bug fixes, and incremental dependency-graph unification for package management.
repositories.emerging_trends:
- **RPC coverage** is being pushed across more commands (`pkg enabled`, registry polling fixed this week; `describe`, `utop`, `tools install`/`exec`, and duplicate watch diagnostics still open) as editor integrations like ocaml-lsp and the VSCode OCaml platform depend on it ([#15589](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/pull/15589), [#15634](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/pull/15634), [#15631](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/15631), [#15608](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/15608), [#15623](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/15623), [#15624](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/15624), [#15609](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/15609))

repositories.brief_summary: Work continued on reference rendering, `[@merlin.hide]` source occurrences, and OxCaml compatibility, all via open, unmerged PRs.
repositories.activity_summary: Three PRs remained open covering reference rendering, source occurrence filtering, and OxCaml fixes, alongside a new OCaml 5.6 support issue.
repositories.activity:
- [Onyeka Obi](https://github.com/MavenRain) opened [#1468](https://github.com/ocaml/odoc/pull/1468), a fix so that references to constructors and record fields (e.g. `{!Bla.Alpha}`) no longer splice the enclosing **type name** into the rendered text, addressing [#372](https://github.com/ocaml/odoc/issues/372); the PR remains open pending a possible follow-up on polymorphic variant tag rendering.
- [Jon Ludlam](https://github.com/jonludlam) opened [#1469](https://github.com/ocaml/odoc/pull/1469), a set of mostly mechanical **OxCaml minus39** compatibility fixes, including switching a function to return an option and use `filter_map` to prepare for handling module types with `with` kind expressions.
- [Benjamin Canou](https://github.com/klakplok) continued work on [#1465](https://github.com/ocaml/odoc/pull/1465) (opened the prior week, discussed further this week), which honours the `[@merlin.hide]` attribute to prevent **spurious source-code links** generated by ppx derivers such as `ppx_deriving`, fixing [#1456](https://github.com/ocaml/odoc/issues/1456).
- [Kate](https://github.com/kit-ty-kate) opened [#1470](https://github.com/ocaml/odoc/issues/1470) flagging that odoc is not yet compatible with the upcoming **OCaml 5.6** release, noting that odoc's dependencies are already available via the opam-alpha-repository for anyone wanting to attempt the port.
repositories.discussions_summary: Reviewers and authors debated edge cases in reference rendering and the choice between `[@merlin.hide]` and ghost locations for suppressing spurious links.
repositories.notable_discussions:
- On [#1468](https://github.com/ocaml/odoc/pull/1468), [Onyeka Obi](https://github.com/MavenRain) and [Paul-Elliot Anglès d'Auriac](https://github.com/panglesd) discussed whether polymorphic variant tags reached through a module (e.g. `Bla.sw.\`On`) should keep the module prefix as a locator or render as a bare tag, and whether tooltips should retain the full type path; both were left unchanged in this PR, deferring to a possible separate follow-up.
- On [#1465](https://github.com/ocaml/odoc/pull/1465), [Benjamin Canou](https://github.com/klakplok) and [Paul-Elliot Anglès d'Auriac](https://github.com/panglesd) discussed why both `[@merlin.hide]` and ghost-location markers are needed to suppress spurious source links, since `ppx_deriving`-generated code uses `[@merlin.hide]` while not consistently following ghost-location conventions, and touched on a possible future refactor sharing this logic with Merlin.
repositories.trends_summary: Continued disclosure of AI-assisted contributions and ongoing attention to OxCaml and upcoming OCaml version compatibility.
repositories.emerging_trends:
- Two of this week's open PRs ([#1468](https://github.com/ocaml/odoc/pull/1468) by [Onyeka Obi](https://github.com/MavenRain) and [#1465](https://github.com/ocaml/odoc/pull/1465) by [Benjamin Canou](https://github.com/klakplok)) explicitly disclose **AI assistance** in their preparation, with authors noting they personally reviewed, built, and tested the changes.
- Compatibility with alternative and upcoming OCaml toolchains remains an active concern, spanning **OxCaml** fixes in [#1469](https://github.com/ocaml/odoc/pull/1469) and the newly opened **OCaml 5.6** tracking issue [#1470](https://github.com/ocaml/odoc/issues/1470).
repositories.contributors_summary: Contributors this week opened new fixes and issues and reviewed reference-rendering and source-occurrence changes.
repositories.contributors:
- [Onyeka Obi](https://github.com/MavenRain) opened [#1468](https://github.com/ocaml/odoc/pull/1468) fixing type-name splicing in constructor and field references, added a cram test suite for the change, updated `CHANGES.md`, and responded to review feedback from [Paul-Elliot Anglès d'Auriac](https://github.com/panglesd) on identifier-pattern simplification.
- [Jon Ludlam](https://github.com/jonludlam) opened [#1469](https://github.com/ocaml/odoc/pull/1469) with a set of OxCaml minus39 compatibility fixes.
- [Benjamin Canou](https://github.com/klakplok) continued discussion on [#1465](https://github.com/ocaml/odoc/pull/1465), explaining the distinction between `[@merlin.hide]` and ghost-location markers in response to reviewer questions.
- [Paul-Elliot Anglès d'Auriac](https://github.com/panglesd) reviewed both [#1468](https://github.com/ocaml/odoc/pull/1468) and [#1465](https://github.com/ocaml/odoc/pull/1465), giving design feedback on reference rendering edge cases and on the `[@merlin.hide]`/ghost-location approach.
- [Kate](https://github.com/kit-ty-kate) opened issue [#1470](https://github.com/ocaml/odoc/issues/1470) raising OCaml 5.6 compatibility.
- [Daniel Bünzli](https://github.com/dbuenzli) is the original reporter of [#372](https://github.com/ocaml/odoc/issues/372), the long-standing reference-rendering issue addressed by [#1468](https://github.com/ocaml/odoc/pull/1468) this week.

repositories.brief_summary: Package documentation server switched from sage to dill with a new build-status link, and the security/library team rosters were updated.
repositories.new_features_summary: New documentation build-status links on package pages after the sage-to-dill docs server migration.
repositories.new_features:
- Package pages now link to a **documentation build status page** on the new docs server: the "No Docs" indicator in the package layout and the documentation-not-found page both link to `package.documentation_status_url` instead of showing a static message or a "Report Missing Docs" GitHub-issue link, by [Jon Ludlam](https://github.com/jonludlam) ([#3716](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml.org/issues/3716))

- Formatting fix for the `doc_status_url`-related comment to satisfy `ocamlformat`, restoring green CI on `main` by [Cuihtlauac Alvarado](https://github.com/cuihtlauac) ([#3730](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml.org/issues/3730))
- Updated `HACKING.md` documentation describing the new `OCAMLORG_DOC_URL`/`OCAMLORG_DOC_STATUS_URL` environment variables and the dill docs pipeline ([#3716](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml.org/issues/3716))

repositories.activity:

- Routine **CI maintenance** merged, bumping the `actions/setup-node` GitHub Action from v6 to v7 ([#2407](https://github.com/ocsigen/js_of_ocaml/pull/2407)).

repositories.brief_summary: AVX-512 support landed in the SIMD backend and closed its tracking issue, alongside Flambda2, reaper/LTO, and quote-metaprogramming work.
repositories.new_features_summary: AVX-512 instruction encoding, -omit-leaf-frame-pointers and -X inlining flags, a new unused-alert-disable warning, and atomic mixed-block fields.
repositories.new_features:
- AVX-512 support landed in the amd64 SIMD backend: [Max Slater](https://github.com/TheNumbat) added the EVEX instruction encoding ([#6294](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6294)) and the opmask/ZMM mask-layout plumbing ([#6293](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6293)), closing the community tracking request for AVX-512 support ([#6257](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6257)); a follow-up PR proposes promoting the new types from `simd_alpha` to `simd_beta` ([#6676](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6676)).
- New `-omit-leaf-frame-pointers` flag (amd64) by [Xavier Clerc](https://github.com/xclerc) skips frame-pointer setup for small leaf functions on `--enable-frame-pointers` builds, where the push/mov/pop sequence was a disproportionate fraction of generated code ([#6679](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6679)).
- New `-X` flag added by [Nathanaëlle Courant](https://github.com/Ekdohibs) to prevent Flambda2 from meeting inlining arguments, implementing [#6616](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6616) ([#6640](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6640)).
- New warning `[unused-alert-disable]` by [Jakub Staroń](https://github.com/staronj) flags `[@alert "-foo"]` disables that no longer suppress any occurrence of the alert, catching attributes that have gone silently stale ([#6524](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6524)).
- Atomic fields in mixed blocks can now be loaded and stored by [Joe Kerrigan](https://github.com/joe-kerrigan), extending atomic-field support beyond flat blocks ([#6545](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6545)).
- `poly_` is now printed in value descriptions by [Zesen Qian](https://github.com/riaqn), improving type output for polymorphic values ([#6446](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6446)).
- **Register allocation** on the backend now uses phi-move information to prioritize coalescing in the IRC allocator, a change by [Xavier Clerc](https://github.com/xclerc) aimed at producing fewer moves in generated code ([#5863](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/5863)).
repositories.activity_summary: 35 PRs opened spanning codegen flags, runtime/effects drafts, and language proposals, alongside merged Flambda2, reaper, quote, and runtime work.
repositories.activity:
- Newly opened work on compiler **flags and codegen** includes a `-thin-library` option from [Stephen Dolan](https://github.com/stedolan) that shrinks `.a`/`.cma` files by referencing rather than embedding `.o`/`.cmo` files ([#6637](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6637)), an `-align-loops` flag from [Jacob Van Buren](https://github.com/jvanburen) to 16-byte-align hot loop headers on amd64 ([#6682](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6682)), a peephole pass folding immediate add/sub into a following `lea` by [Xavier Clerc](https://github.com/xclerc) ([#6680](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6680)), better cost modelling for `csel`/`cmov` selection by [@ttebbi-janestreet](https://github.com/ttebbi-janestreet) ([#6659](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6659)), and a draft `-no-trans-deps` flag from [Zesen Qian](https://github.com/riaqn) for direct-only import tables ([#6660](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6660)).
- Runtime and **effects/fiber** work opened this week includes proof-of-concept PRs from [Nick Barnes](https://github.com/NickBarnes) to move systhreads into the runtime ([#6642](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6642)) and split the runtime ([#6645](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6645)), a draft on lexical fiber parents from [Max Slater](https://github.com/TheNumbat) ([#6652](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6652)), and a fix from [Aspen Smith](https://github.com/glittershark) for yielding inference on `Stdlib.Effect.Shallow.fiber` ([#6675](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6675)).
- Typing and language-surface proposals opened include draft support for **variant subtype declarations** (`type t :> u`) from [Luke Maurer](https://github.com/lukemaurer) ([#6655](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6655)), a draft on first-class modalities (`t @@ m` as a type) from [@julesjacobs](https://github.com/julesjacobs) ([#6678](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6678)), layout polymorphism over records/variants with `[any]`-fields from [Ryan Tjoa](https://github.com/rtjoa) ([#6687](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6687), [#6688](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6688)), delayed constraint addition on allocation/locality mode axes from [@zhizhuoxin](https://github.com/zhizhuoxin) ([#6671](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6671)), a fix to skip the vacuous nongen check for persistent `module type of` from [@julesjacobs](https://github.com/julesjacobs) ([#6685](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6685)), and a change disallowing `max_int + 1` from silently overflowing to `min_int` in int literals from [James Rayman](https://github.com/jra4) ([#6670](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6670)).
- Link-time-optimization work continues with a draft from [Miriam Vellacott](https://github.com/mirivella) to store resumable reaper state in CMR files ([#6641](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6641)), following the reaper stage-splitting and new `reaper-rebuild`/`reaper-solve` entry points merged this week ([#6627](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6627), [#6632](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6632), [#6656](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6656), [#6638](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6638)).
- Testing and CI improvements opened include a way to run the testsuite against the boot compiler from [Nathanaëlle Courant](https://github.com/Ekdohibs) ([#6665](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6665)), a CI check for new `XXX` comments from [Luke Maurer](https://github.com/lukemaurer) ([#6662](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6662)), and draft validation of the CFG reachability pass from [@hwasilewskijs](https://github.com/hwasilewskijs) ([#6673](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6673)); a related fix merged this week prevents stale binary-emitter files from causing spurious CI verification failures, with test infrastructure credited to Claude ([#6658](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6658)).
- Merlin tooling saw multiple new PRs from [Liam Stevenson](https://github.com/liam923) syncing Merlin for `5.4.0-ox4` and unmerging comments ([#6683](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6683), [#6684](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6684)), plus a draft merging Merlin's typing recovery from OCaml 5.4.1 by [Ulysse](https://github.com/voodoos) ([#6674](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6674)); this follows Merlin synchronization changes and `ocaml-index` staleness fixes merged earlier in the week ([#6563](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6563), [#6654](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6654)).
- A cluster of **quote/metaprogramming** cleanups by [Jakub Bachurski](https://github.com/jbachurski) merged this week: consistent internal naming for quotes and splices ([#6575](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6575)), refactored quoting of predefined names with `code` renamed to `expr` internally ([#6635](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6635), [#6576](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6576)), mode-constraint fixes in quotes ([#6647](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6647)), and support for unboxed literals in quotes ([#6650](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6650)).
- **Flambda2** saw a batch of merges from [Basile Clément](https://github.com/bclement-ocp) and [Vincent Laviron](https://github.com/lthls): a breadth-first meet strategy ([#6191](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6191), closing [#6581](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6581)), consistent ordering of extra parameters from dataflow ([#6653](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6653)), handling of coercions in `make_suitable_for_environment` ([#6639](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6639), closing [#6584](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6584)), an identity fix for name-mode-to-int conversion ([#6431](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6431)), allocation-free rule evaluation in datalog via `Or_null` ([#6377](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6377)), removal of mutable-string support ([#6570](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6570)), and a fix from [Pierre Chambart](https://github.com/chambart) allowing simplification of stubs without size blowup ([#5496](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/5496)).
- Runtime fixes from [Nick Barnes](https://github.com/NickBarnes) merged this week: a race-condition crash fix in the signal handler ([#6342](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6342)), atomic bigarray proxy creation ([#6344](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6344)), frametable measurement tooling ([#6487](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6487)), and a `make promote` fix for Dune 3.23 ([#6544](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6544)).
- Bytecode/effects instrumentation from [Aspen Smith](https://github.com/glittershark) merged: recording of unyielding calls in bytecode debug events ([#6251](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6251)) and yielding info on method sends ([#6661](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6661)), alongside a de-flake fix for `handle_tick_raises.ml` ([#6664](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6664)).
- The dissector tool was hardened by [Simon Spies](https://github.com/spiessimon) (linking only relevant compilation units, [#6526](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6526)) and [Jakub Staroń](https://github.com/staronj) (robustness to manifest-resolved link inputs, [#6501](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6501)).
- Typing work merged from [Max Slater](https://github.com/TheNumbat) (guarding unsigned types behind the `small_numbers` extension, [#6634](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6634)), [Ryan Tjoa](https://github.com/rtjoa) (removing unnecessary `caml_modify` calls via better value kinds for type variables, [#6633](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6633)), [Zesen Qian](https://github.com/riaqn) (generic mode-axis exhaustion in `out_type` and expected staticity on `Texp_ident`, [#6569](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6569), [#6630](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6630)), and [Jack Rickard](https://github.com/Skepfyr) (splitting kind templates' env mode and alloc mode, [#6636](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6636)).
- Housekeeping merges include a magic-number bump for the `5.4.0-ox4` release by [James Rayman](https://github.com/jra4) ([#6668](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6668)), a `default.nix` update for newer nixpkgs by [Jacob Van Buren](https://github.com/jvanburen) ([#6573](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6573)), and `Unix_for_owee` wiring in `driver/boot_ocamlopt.ml` by [Basile Clément](https://github.com/bclement-ocp) ([#6646](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6646)).
repositories.discussions_summary: AVX-512 request closed by its own author once implemented; design discussion on naked immediates and inlining-flag naming.
repositories.notable_discussions:
- [Zane Hambly](https://github.com/Zaneham)'s AVX-512 proposal ([#6257](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6257)) prompted implementation rather than debate: the author closed it themselves once the encoding and mask-layout PRs landed, noting "it is the subject of a few PR's now."
- On [#6619](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6619) (extensions on naked immediates), [Basile Clément](https://github.com/bclement-ocp) explained the motivation is recovering match information destroyed by the switcher pass, and that discussion converged on first trying to disable switcher before Flambda2 as a simpler initial step.
- Review discussion on the new `-X` inlining-meet flag ([#6640](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6640)) centered on naming clarity, with [Basile Clément](https://github.com/bclement-ocp) pushing back on ambiguous `current`/`other` parameter names and asking for test constraints to be documented in one place rather than split across `with_meet.ml` and `without_meet.ml`.
repositories.trends_summary: SIMD investment compounding, exploratory runtime-restructuring drafts, and sequential consistency passes over quotes and reaper/LTO code.
repositories.emerging_trends:
- SIMD backend investment continued to compound, moving from AVX-512 encoding infrastructure ([#6294](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6294), [#6293](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6293)) toward beta-stabilizing the new types ([#6676](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6676)) in the same week the original request issue closed ([#6257](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6257)).
- Several contributors are opening exploratory/draft PRs for larger runtime restructuring — systhreads-into-runtime ([#6642](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6642)) and a runtime split ([#6645](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6645)) from [Nick Barnes](https://github.com/NickBarnes), and lexical fiber parents from [Max Slater](https://github.com/TheNumbat) ([#6652](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6652)) — suggesting active design exploration on the effects/runtime boundary rather than incremental fixes.
- The quote/metaprogramming subsystem is undergoing a consistency pass (naming, mode constraints, unboxed literals) by [Jakub Bachurski](https://github.com/jbachurski) across several small, sequential PRs ([#6575](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6575), [#6635](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6635), [#6647](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6647), [#6650](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6650), [#6576](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6576)) rather than one large change.
- Link-time optimization (reaper) work is shifting toward resumability, with a new file format and CMR-based state storage ([#6638](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6638), [#6641](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6641)) following the earlier split into staged passes ([#6627](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6627), [#6632](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6632)).

repositories.brief_summary: Path handling moved to per-backend implementations, directory traversal sped up, and an empty-path fs bug fixed.
repositories.new_features_summary: Directory traversal speedup, backend-specific path split/join, and a fix for empty-path fs operations on eio_posix.
repositories.new_features:
- Directory traversal on large directories sped up by increasing the `getdents64` stack buffer from `PATH_MAX + sizeof(dirent64)` to a fixed 65536 bytes, cutting the number of syscalls needed by an order of magnitude for roughly 30% faster traversal of directories with around a million files, and helping network filesystems too, by [Anil Madhavapeddy](https://github.com/avsm) ([#910](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/pull/910))
- **Path splitting and joining** moved out of the frontend into per-backend `Eio.Fs.Pi.PATH` implementations, with a new `Eio_utils.Posix_path` module providing the POSIX behavior, laying groundwork for Windows-specific path support by [Thomas Leonard](https://github.com/talex5) ([#913](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/pull/913))
- `Eio.Path.split` for POSIX paths reworked to scan the string directly instead of allocating intermediate lists, reducing allocation for path splitting by [Thomas Leonard](https://github.com/talex5) ([#915](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/pull/915))
- Fixed `fstat`, `mkdir`, symlink creation/reading, `chmod`, `chown` and directory listing failing on `eio_posix` when applied directly to an unconfined `fs` handle because `fstatat(AT_FDCWD, "", ...)` rejects empty paths, which also resolves [Eio.Path.mkdirs failing on a relative path whose first component doesn't exist](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/906), by [Thomas Leonard](https://github.com/talex5) ([#907](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/pull/907), fixes [#906](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/906))
- Documentation for `Eio.Path.( / )` and `Eio.Path.split` updated to clarify their behavior is POSIX-specific, anticipating different semantics once Windows support lands ([#913](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/pull/913))
repositories.activity_summary: New drafts target 32-bit build fixes, Windows path support, and device mknod, while path-backend and empty-path fixes merged.
repositories.activity:
- Newly opened PRs awaiting review include a fix for the **32-bit build**, where `MSG_CMSG_CLOEXEC` overflowed OCaml's native int on 32-bit platforms, by [Thomas Leonard](https://github.com/talex5) ([#917](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/pull/917), addressing [#909](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/909)); a draft implementing `Eio.Path.native` as a **backend interface with Windows support**, split off from a larger patch, by [Thomas Leonard](https://github.com/talex5) ([#916](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/pull/916)); a draft adding **device `mknod` support** for creating device files beyond FIFOs by [Anil Madhavapeddy](https://github.com/avsm) ([#911](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/pull/911)); and the original **Windows path-handling** draft it was split from, currently marked as conflicting, also by [Anil Madhavapeddy](https://github.com/avsm) ([#908](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/pull/908))
- The **Windows path support** effort saw back-and-forth between [Anil Madhavapeddy](https://github.com/avsm) and [Thomas Leonard](https://github.com/talex5) over path normalisation, the meaning of `of_native`, and per-drive versus per-process working directories, converging on treating paths lexically and possibly rejecting drive-relative paths like `C:foo` ([#908](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/pull/908), [#916](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/pull/916))
- The **device `mknod`** draft prompted discussion on sharing the feature with `eio_linux`, introducing a portable `Eio.File.Dev.t` type, and handling device numbers on platforms like Wayland where they don't fit a fixed-width field, between [Anil Madhavapeddy](https://github.com/avsm) and [Thomas Leonard](https://github.com/talex5) ([#911](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/pull/911))
- Merged this week: the **path-backend refactor** ([#913](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/pull/913)), the **posix split allocation optimisation** ([#915](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/pull/915)), the **getdents buffer** speedup ([#910](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/pull/910)), and the **empty-path fix** for unconfined fs operations ([#907](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/pull/907)), which resolved [#906](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/906)
repositories.discussions_summary: 32-bit platform support, directory fsync, and zero-allocation tracing were debated across three issues.
repositories.notable_discussions:
- [Build fails on 32-bit architectures](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/909) sparked debate on whether Eio should support 32-bit at all: [Thomas Leonard](https://github.com/talex5) suggested restricting `eio.unix` to 64-bit only, [Stéphane Glondu](https://github.com/glondu) noted Debian still officially supports armhf and i386, and [Anil Madhavapeddy](https://github.com/avsm) proposed following OCaml upstream's guidance of bytecode-only on 32-bit, which [#917](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/pull/917) later addressed pragmatically
- [Trace events allocate 23 words each while the ring is active](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/914) traced an allocation in `Eio.Private.Trace` back to `Runtime_events.User.write`; [Thomas Gazagnaire](https://github.com/samoht) reported the repro, [Thomas Leonard](https://github.com/talex5) pinpointed an unnecessary closure allocation in upstream `runtime_events.ml`, and [Anil Madhavapeddy](https://github.com/avsm) is benchmarking a single-buffer fix, referencing an upstream OCaml commit and looping in [Sadiq Jaffer](https://github.com/sadiqj)
- [No way to sync a directory](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/912) raised the need for directory `fsync` to make journal-then-rename patterns durable in an embedded database; [Anil Madhavapeddy](https://github.com/avsm) agreed a path-based `sync` in `Fs.Pi.DIR` is reasonable and noted `fdatasync` may also be needed
repositories.trends_summary: Path handling is being split into POSIX/Windows backends, alongside renewed attention to portability and allocation profiling.
repositories.emerging_trends:
- Path handling is being restructured into backend-specific modules (POSIX now, Windows next) rather than one shared implementation, spanning [#908](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/pull/908), [#913](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/pull/913), [#915](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/pull/915), and [#916](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/pull/916)
- Large draft PRs are being split into smaller reviewable pieces, as with [Anil Madhavapeddy](https://github.com/avsm)'s [#908](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/pull/908) being carved into [#913](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/pull/913), [#915](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/pull/915), and [#916](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/pull/916)
- Renewed focus on portability edge cases and allocation profiling of hot paths, seen in the 32-bit build issue and fix ([#909](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/909), [#917](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/pull/917)) and the tracing/`getdents`/path-split allocation work ([#914](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/914), [#910](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/pull/910), [#915](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/pull/915))
repositories.contributors_summary: Two contributors were active in code, review, and issue discussion, with three others filing detailed issue reports.
repositories.contributors:

group_summaries.new_features:
- **[ocaml/dune](https://github.com/ocaml/dune)**: added an `--include-empty` flag to `dune describe external-lib-deps` so dependency-free libraries are still listed, by [Nat Karmios](https://github.com/NatKarmios) ([ocaml/dune#15585](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/15585), fixes [ocaml/dune#15566](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/15566)); fixed a rule/alias bug that leaked actions between aliases on target-less multi-alias rules, by Nat Karmios ([ocaml/dune#15581](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/15581), fixes [ocaml/dune#15576](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/15576)); `dune pkg enabled` now queries a running RPC server for transient `--pkg enabled`/`disabled` settings, by [Ali Caglayan](https://github.com/Alizter) ([ocaml/dune#15589](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/15589)); fixed RPC registry polling to reliably rescan on mtime changes so clients like ocaml-lsp discover new instances, by [Rudi Grinberg](https://github.com/rgrinberg) ([ocaml/dune#15634](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/15634)); added Windows `Proc.wait` support for the typed process API ([ocaml/dune#15536](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/15536)); and roughly halved time/allocation for module alias generation via `String_builder`, by [Antonio Nuno Monteiro](https://github.com/anmonteiro) ([ocaml/dune#15657](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/15657))
- **[ocaml/merlin](https://github.com/ocaml/merlin)**: released **5.8.1**, fixing ocaml-index staleness detection for ppx-preprocessed files ([ocaml/merlin#2110](https://github.com/ocaml/merlin/issues/2110)) by [Liam Stevenson](https://github.com/liam923), a load_path invalidation race across concurrent typer instances ([ocaml/merlin#2109](https://github.com/ocaml/merlin/issues/2109)), and a `document` query that returned a neighboring constructor's or field's doc comment ([ocaml/merlin#2092](https://github.com/ocaml/merlin/issues/2092)) by Liam Stevenson; also published a **5.8.1-506~preview** build with experimental OCaml 5.6 support (https://github.com/ocaml/merlin/releases/tag/v5.8.1-506_preview)
- **[ocaml/ocaml-lsp](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp)**: function-parameter inlay hints are now **enabled by default** ([ocaml/ocaml-lsp#2097](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/2097), fixes [ocaml/ocaml-lsp#1371](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/1371)); inline code-action edits now resolve **lazily** for supporting clients ([ocaml/ocaml-lsp#1808](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/1808)); semantic-token capability negotiation now respects client-declared token types/modifiers ([ocaml/ocaml-lsp#1860](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/1860), fixes [ocaml/ocaml-lsp#1138](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/1138)); a large batch of completion, rename, and signature-help correctness fixes landed ([ocaml/ocaml-lsp#1964](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/1964), [ocaml/ocaml-lsp#1966](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/1966), [ocaml/ocaml-lsp#1987](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/1987)); and a FreeBSD build failure from a misplaced `statfs(2)` header was fixed, by [emre](https://github.com/dayangac) ([ocaml/ocaml-lsp#2070](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/2070), fixes [ocaml/ocaml-lsp#1069](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/1069)); all remaining items by [Rudi Grinberg](https://github.com/rgrinberg)

group_summaries.new_features_summary: AVX-512 SIMD support, new compiler flags, atomic mixed-block fields in oxcaml, and a fixed utop package in opam-repository.
group_summaries.new_features:
- **[oxcaml/oxcaml](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml)**: AVX-512 support landed in the amd64 SIMD backend — [Max Slater](https://github.com/TheNumbat) added the EVEX instruction encoding ([oxcaml/oxcaml#6294](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6294)) and opmask/ZMM mask-layout plumbing ([oxcaml/oxcaml#6293](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6293)), closing the community tracking request ([oxcaml/oxcaml#6257](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6257)); a follow-up proposes promoting the new types from `simd_alpha` to `simd_beta` ([oxcaml/oxcaml#6676](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6676)).
- **[oxcaml/oxcaml](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml)**: new `-omit-leaf-frame-pointers` flag by [Xavier Clerc](https://github.com/xclerc) skips frame-pointer setup for small leaf functions on `--enable-frame-pointers` builds ([oxcaml/oxcaml#6679](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6679)); new `-X` flag by [Nathanaëlle Courant](https://github.com/Ekdohibs) prevents Flambda2 from meeting inlining arguments ([oxcaml/oxcaml#6640](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6640)).
- **[oxcaml/oxcaml](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml)**: new `[unused-alert-disable]` warning by [Jakub Staroń](https://github.com/staronj) flags stale `[@alert "-foo"]` disables ([oxcaml/oxcaml#6524](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6524)); atomic fields in mixed blocks can now be loaded and stored, by [Joe Kerrigan](https://github.com/joe-kerrigan) ([oxcaml/oxcaml#6545](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6545)).
- **[oxcaml/opam-repository](https://github.com/oxcaml/opam-repository)**: added `utop.2.16.0+ox2`, restoring installability against OxCaml 5.2.0minus39, and migrated the CI test matrix to Warp-hosted runners ([oxcaml/opam-repository#58](https://github.com/oxcaml/opam-repository/issues/58), [oxcaml/opam-repository#57](https://github.com/oxcaml/opam-repository/issues/57)).
group_summaries.group_overview:

group_summaries.activity:
- **Compiler flags/codegen** ([oxcaml/oxcaml](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml)): newly opened work includes a `-thin-library` option from [Stephen Dolan](https://github.com/stedolan) to shrink `.a`/`.cma` files ([oxcaml/oxcaml#6637](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6637)), an `-align-loops` flag from [Jacob Van Buren](https://github.com/jvanburen) ([oxcaml/oxcaml#6682](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6682)), a peephole pass folding add/sub into `lea` from [Xavier Clerc](https://github.com/xclerc) ([oxcaml/oxcaml#6680](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6680)), and better `csel`/`cmov` cost modelling from [@ttebbi-janestreet](https://github.com/ttebbi-janestreet) ([oxcaml/oxcaml#6659](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6659)).
- **Runtime/effects** ([oxcaml/oxcaml](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml)): proof-of-concept drafts from [Nick Barnes](https://github.com/NickBarnes) on moving systhreads into the runtime ([oxcaml/oxcaml#6642](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6642)) and splitting the runtime ([oxcaml/oxcaml#6645](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6645)), a draft on lexical fiber parents from [Max Slater](https://github.com/TheNumbat) ([oxcaml/oxcaml#6652](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6652)), and a yielding-inference fix from [Aspen Smith](https://github.com/glittershark) ([oxcaml/oxcaml#6675](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6675)).

- **Quote/metaprogramming** ([oxcaml/oxcaml](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml)): a sequence of consistency cleanups by [Jakub Bachurski](https://github.com/jbachurski) merged, covering naming, mode-constraint fixes, and unboxed literal support ([oxcaml/oxcaml#6575](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6575), [oxcaml/oxcaml#6635](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6635), [oxcaml/oxcaml#6647](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6647), [oxcaml/oxcaml#6650](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6650), [oxcaml/oxcaml#6576](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6576)).
- **Flambda2** ([oxcaml/oxcaml](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml)): [Basile Clément](https://github.com/bclement-ocp) and [Vincent Laviron](https://github.com/lthls) merged a breadth-first meet strategy ([oxcaml/oxcaml#6191](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6191), closing [oxcaml/oxcaml#6581](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6581)), coercion handling in `make_suitable_for_environment` ([oxcaml/oxcaml#6639](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6639), closing [oxcaml/oxcaml#6584](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6584)), and removal of mutable-string support ([oxcaml/oxcaml#6570](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6570)).
- **Runtime fixes** ([oxcaml/oxcaml](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml)): [Nick Barnes](https://github.com/NickBarnes) merged a signal-handler race crash fix ([oxcaml/oxcaml#6342](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6342)), atomic bigarray proxy creation ([oxcaml/oxcaml#6344](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6344)), and a `make promote` fix for Dune 3.23 ([oxcaml/oxcaml#6544](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6544)).
