group_summaries.new_features:
- Typechecking-performance work on the `js_of_ocaml`/Lwt compilation-time blowup continued, with **occurs-check elision** for fresh type variables during instantiation by [Stefan Muenzel](https://github.com/smuenzel) cutting the offending file from 10 minutes to 5 seconds ([ocaml/ocaml#14913](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14913)), and further **type-path equivalence normalization** optimizations by [Gabriel Scherer](https://github.com/gasche) merged via [ocaml/ocaml#14952](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14952) (building on [ocaml/ocaml#14947](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14947) and [ocaml/ocaml#14950](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14950)), bringing the same case down to 170ms ([ocaml/ocaml#14897](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14897)).
- Stdlib additions: `Dynarray.append_iarray` and `Pqueue.of_iarray` by [Nicolás Ojeda Bär](https://github.com/nojb) close a gap for converting immutable arrays without unsafe code ([ocaml/ocaml#14909](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14909), fixes [ocaml/ocaml#14320](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14320)), and `Option.try_value`/`Result.try_value` were added ([ocaml/ocaml#14941](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14941)).
- Fixed a pattern-matching **switch overflow** bug where the integer-overflow guard failed to account for `abs min_int = min_int`, by [Florian Angeletti](https://github.com/Octachron) ([ocaml/ocaml#14890](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14890)).
- Fixed a **memory leak** in the runtime caused by an unbounded internal cache of stacks ([ocaml/ocaml#14940](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14940)).
- Fixed the generated compiler-cloning script used by opam to work inside opam's sandbox on macOS, where an old bash version broke here-document handling, by [David Allsopp](https://github.com/dra27) ([ocaml/ocaml#14923](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14923)).
- `OCAMLTOP_INCLUDE_PATH` is now ignored during the build, preventing environment leakage into build steps ([ocaml/ocaml#14871](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14871), [ocaml/ocaml#14914](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14914)).
- Fixed a docstring typo in `Bigarray.Array2.init` that reversed the description of `dim1`/`dim2`, by [Tristan F.-R.](https://github.com/tristan-f-r) ([ocaml/ocaml#14973](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14973)).
- Added documentation on the ocamllex `-w` command-line argument to the man page ([ocaml/ocaml#14902](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14902), [ocaml/ocaml#14944](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14944)).
group_summaries.group_overview:
- Activity this week was concentrated entirely in [ocaml/ocaml](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml); [ocaml/RFCs](https://github.com/ocaml/RFCs) recorded no repository activity.
- A coordinated multi-contributor effort resolved a typechecker performance pathology surfaced by js_of_ocaml/Lwt builds, cutting compilation time on the offending file from 10 minutes to 170ms ([ocaml/ocaml#14897](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14897), [ocaml/ocaml#14913](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14913), [ocaml/ocaml#14952](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14952)).
- Nine new PRs were opened, spanning native atomics, a new `Hashtbl` implementation, win32/`Sys` fixes, and stdlib proposals.
- Design discussion continued on a new `Hashtbl` implementation for deterministic iteration order, feeding a broader RFC discussion on hash-flooding protection ([ocaml/ocaml#14956](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14956), [ocaml/ocaml#14967](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/discussions/14967)).
- Build-system and POWER-architecture maintenance continued alongside stdlib additions such as `Dynarray.append_iarray` ([ocaml/ocaml#14909](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14909)) and a runtime memory-leak fix ([ocaml/ocaml#14940](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14940)).
group_summaries.activity_summary: Nine PRs opened covering native atomics, Hashtbl design, and win32/Sys fixes, while typechecker-performance, POWER, and build work continued.
group_summaries.activity:
- Nine PRs opened this week span runtime, typing, and stdlib work: [Zane Hambly](https://github.com/Zaneham) proposed generating native atomic `exchange`/`compare_and_set` instructions across all five backends, replacing C calls with inline assembly on amd64/arm64/riscv/power/s390x ([ocaml/ocaml#14980](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14980)); [Gabriel Scherer](https://github.com/gasche) opened a re-implementation of `Weak.Make` hashsets using open-addressing with linear probing, reporting a 30% speedup on alt-ergo-free ([ocaml/ocaml#14979](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14979)); [314eter](https://github.com/314eter) proposed fixing `with module type` precedence so `=` and `:=` behave consistently, a breaking change for existing uses of the old precedence ([ocaml/ocaml#14978](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14978)); [Romain Beauxis](https://github.com/toots) fixed a win32 select handle leak reported by liquidsoap users ([ocaml/ocaml#14975](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14975)); [Khalid](https://github.com/khalidbelk) proposed `Sys.filepath_exists` as a safer alternative to `Sys.file_exists` ([ocaml/ocaml#14974](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14974)); [Gabriel Scherer](https://github.com/gasche) proposed enabling `-g` by default in the bytecode compiler to close the debugging gap with `ocamlopt` ([ocaml/ocaml#14971](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14971)); [Tim McGilchrist](https://github.com/tmcgilchrist) opened two runtime-events fixes, correcting a `minor_allocated_bytes` unit-conversion bug ([ocaml/ocaml#14969](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14969)) and adding a missing `EV_MINOR_EPHE_CLEAN` constructor that crashed consumers on out-of-range values ([ocaml/ocaml#14966](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14966)); [Xavier Van de Woestyne](https://github.com/xvw) continued the typing-recovery work needed for Merlin ([ocaml/ocaml#14963](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14963)); and [Török Edwin](https://github.com/edwintorok) opened a draft exposing that `Atomic.t` is not a float in the interface to improve code generation ([ocaml/ocaml#14977](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14977), following [ocaml/ocaml#14976](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14976)).
- The **typechecker path-equivalence and occurs-check performance work** triggered by [ocaml/ocaml#14897](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14897) (js_of_ocaml compile-time blowup) was resolved this week through coordinated contributions from [Stefan Muenzel](https://github.com/smuenzel) ([ocaml/ocaml#14900](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14900), [ocaml/ocaml#14913](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14913)) and [Gabriel Scherer](https://github.com/gasche)/[Florian Angeletti](https://github.com/Octachron) ([ocaml/ocaml#14927](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14927), [ocaml/ocaml#14947](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14947), [ocaml/ocaml#14950](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14950), [ocaml/ocaml#14952](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14952)), taking typechecking time on the offending file from 10 minutes to 170ms.
- Ongoing **native atomics** work builds on the earlier fetch-and-add landing ([ocaml/ocaml#14575](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14575)), with [Zane Hambly](https://github.com/Zaneham)'s new `exchange`/`compare_and_set` PR ([ocaml/ocaml#14980](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14980)) discussing a follow-up to unify with [Gabriel Scherer](https://github.com/gasche)'s proposed `compare_and_exchange` ([ocaml/ocaml#14912](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14912)), while [Török Edwin](https://github.com/edwintorok) separately proposes exposing that `Atomic.t` excludes floats for better inlining ([ocaml/ocaml#14977](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14977)).
- Extensive design discussion continued on a **new `Hashtbl` implementation** guaranteeing deterministic iteration order by [Jeannalyse](https://github.com/Jeannalyse) ([ocaml/ocaml#14956](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14956)), with detailed benchmarking trade-offs explored by [Gabriel Scherer](https://github.com/gasche) and [Stefan Muenzel](https://github.com/smuenzel), feeding into the broader RFC ([ocaml/ocaml#14967](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/discussions/14967)) and the older randomized-seeding proposal by [Hannes Mehnert](https://github.com/hannesm) ([ocaml/ocaml#14291](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14291)).
- POWER-architecture support continued with [Tim McGilchrist](https://github.com/tmcgilchrist)'s frame-pointer PR nearing review completion after feedback from [Olivier Nicole](https://github.com/OlivierNicole) and [Zane Hambly](https://github.com/Zaneham) ([ocaml/ocaml#14505](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14505)).
- Build/CI maintenance merged this week: reverting a temporary MSVC warning suppression now that the upstream issue is fixed, by [David Allsopp](https://github.com/dra27) ([ocaml/ocaml#14103](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14103)); disabling the parsetree-compatibility bot on forks ([ocaml/ocaml#14972](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14972)); and a tooling fix for missing trailing output in expect tests, by [Stefan Muenzel](https://github.com/smuenzel) ([ocaml/ocaml#14959](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14959)).
- [David Allsopp](https://github.com/dra27) continued build-system work in progress, including sanitizing environment variables from the build ([ocaml/ocaml#14915](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14915)), switching the required autoconf version to 2.72 ([ocaml/ocaml#14953](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14953)), merging `Dynlink` into a single module ahead of a later refactor ([ocaml/ocaml#14970](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14970)), and trunk-compiler support for `ocaml-system` in opam ([ocaml/ocaml#14354](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14354)).
- [Florian Angeletti](https://github.com/Octachron)'s long-running **structured compiler diagnostics** proposal remained under active review ([ocaml/ocaml#13766](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/13766)), alongside [Alistair](https://github.com/johnyob)'s `type_approx` refactor series ([ocaml/ocaml#14538](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14538), [ocaml/ocaml#14517](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14517)) and labeled-tuple-projection proposal ([ocaml/ocaml#14257](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14257)).
- [shym](https://github.com/shym) continued work supporting relocatable cross compilers ([ocaml/ocaml#14929](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14929)), and [Nat Mote](https://github.com/nmote) validated a fix for `sigaltstack` failures with musl on certain Intel CPUs, confirmed on hardware and reported upstream to musl maintainers ([ocaml/ocaml#14933](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14933)).
- [Samuel Vivien](https://github.com/samsa1)'s proposal to make `unify` return a `result` instead of raising was confirmed ready to merge pending a rebase ([ocaml/ocaml#14425](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14425)).
- [Stefan Muenzel](https://github.com/smuenzel) shared coq-bench numbers showing a `caml_apply` inlining change reducing runtime by up to 25% on function-call-heavy workloads ([ocaml/ocaml#14925](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14925)), and [Gabriel Scherer](https://github.com/gasche) proposed a refactor to consolidate repeated path-compression logic ([ocaml/ocaml#14910](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14910)).
- [Nick Barnes](https://github.com/NickBarnes) posted a proof-of-concept moving systhreads into the runtime, eliminating the largely-fictional separation between the two ([ocaml/ocaml#14965](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14965)).
- Pending stdlib proposals under discussion include [Brian Ward](https://github.com/WardBrian)'s `Result.all`/`Option.all` for collapsing lists of optional/result values ([ocaml/ocaml#14964](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14964)), [Benoit](https://github.com/benjub)'s `Char.Ascii.is_punct` ([ocaml/ocaml#14957](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14957), ultimately recommended for closure by [Daniel Bünzli](https://github.com/dbuenzli)), and [Jeannalyse](https://github.com/Jeannalyse)'s `Dynarray.sort`/`stable_sort` ([ocaml/ocaml#14848](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14848)).
- [Khalid](https://github.com/khalidbelk)'s earlier `Sys.file_exists'` proposal was closed in favor of the stdlib team's `filepath_exists` design, now implemented in [ocaml/ocaml#14974](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14974) ([ocaml/ocaml#14951](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14951)), and [Gabriel Scherer](https://github.com/gasche)'s `Reoptimize ocamlc -g` PR was closed after [Vincent Laviron](https://github.com/lthls) warned it could degrade the bytecode-debugger experience, redirected into [ocaml/ocaml#14971](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14971).
group_summaries.notable_discussions:
- [Make unlabeled applications fine again?](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/discussions/14968) by [Gabriel Scherer](https://github.com/gasche) revisits whether OCaml's existing (but discouraged since warning 6) support for calling labeled functions unlabeled could ease adding labels to existing APIs without breaking callers, spun out of the `Atomic.compare_and_exchange` labeling debate ([ocaml/ocaml#14912](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14912)).
- [RFC: Hashtbl: remember insertion order to guarantee deterministic iteration](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/discussions/14967) by [Gabriel Scherer](https://github.com/gasche) proposes an internal doubly-linked list to make `Hashtbl` iteration deterministic even with randomized seeding, weighing a roughly 42% memory overhead against enabling hash-flooding protection by default, with alternatives (a new `Hashmap` module, Go-style intentional randomization) surveyed against Python/PHP/Ruby/Java precedent; it directly informs [ocaml/ocaml#14956](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14956) and [ocaml/ocaml#14291](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14291).
group_summaries.emerging_trends:
- Sustained focus on **typechecker performance pathologies** surfaced by real-world dune-wrapped libraries (js_of_ocaml/Lwt), resolved through a chain of coordinated PRs from multiple contributors within the same week ([ocaml/ocaml#14897](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14897), [ocaml/ocaml#14913](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14913), [ocaml/ocaml#14927](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14927), [ocaml/ocaml#14947](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14947), [ocaml/ocaml#14950](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14950), [ocaml/ocaml#14952](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14952)).
- Growing interest in exposing more **native/inline atomic primitives** at the assembly level rather than through C calls, spanning fetch-and-add (landed earlier), exchange/CAS ([ocaml/ocaml#14980](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14980)), and compare-and-exchange ([ocaml/ocaml#14912](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14912)), each requiring careful cross-architecture fence and memory-model review.
- Multiple concurrent proposals for improving `Hashtbl` security and predictability ([ocaml/ocaml#14291](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14291), [ocaml/ocaml#14956](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14956), [ocaml/ocaml#14967](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/discussions/14967)) show the standard library team weighing performance and memory trade-offs carefully before committing to a default-seeding change.
- Disclosed LLM-assisted contributions are becoming more visible in PR descriptions, for example a bug investigation credited to LLM assistance in [ocaml/ocaml#14975](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14975) and disclosed LLM use per OCaml's AI policy in [ocaml/ocaml#14933](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14933).

group_summaries.brief_summary: Eio split path handling into per-backend modules and sped up directory traversal; ocaml-uring triaged a Debian flaky-test report.
group_summaries.new_features_summary: Eio sped up directory traversal ~30%, moved path split/join per-backend, and fixed empty-path fs failures on eio_posix.
group_summaries.new_features:
- Directory traversal sped up roughly 30% on directories with around a million files by increasing the `getdents64` stack buffer from `PATH_MAX + sizeof(dirent64)` to a fixed 65536 bytes, cutting syscalls by an order of magnitude and also helping network filesystems, by [Anil Madhavapeddy](https://github.com/avsm) ([ocaml-multicore/eio#910](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/910))
- Path splitting and joining moved out of the frontend into per-backend `Eio.Fs.Pi.PATH` implementations, with a new `Eio_utils.Posix_path` module providing POSIX behavior and laying groundwork for Windows-specific path support, by [Thomas Leonard](https://github.com/talex5) ([ocaml-multicore/eio#913](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/913))
- `Eio.Path.split` for POSIX paths reworked to scan the string directly instead of allocating intermediate lists, reducing allocation, by [Thomas Leonard](https://github.com/talex5) ([ocaml-multicore/eio#915](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/915))
- Fixed `fstat`, `mkdir`, symlink creation/reading, `chmod`, `chown` and directory listing failing on `eio_posix` when applied directly to an unconfined `fs` handle, since `fstatat(AT_FDCWD, "", ...)` rejects empty paths, by [Thomas Leonard](https://github.com/talex5) ([ocaml-multicore/eio#907](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/907), fixes [ocaml-multicore/eio#906](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/906))
group_summaries.group_overview:

- [ocaml-multicore/ocaml-uring](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/ocaml-uring) had no commits merged; activity was limited to a single issue thread about a Debian-packaging test failure ([ocaml-multicore/ocaml-uring#161](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/ocaml-uring/issues/161))
- [ocaml-multicore/domainslib](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/domainslib), [ocaml-multicore/meio](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/meio), [ocaml-multicore/saturn](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/saturn), [ocaml-multicore/eio-trace](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio-trace), [ocaml-multicore/picos](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/picos), [ocaml-multicore/kcas](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/kcas), and [ocaml-multicore/ocaml-iomux](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/ocaml-iomux) recorded no activity for this period
group_summaries.activity_summary: Eio advanced Windows path and 32-bit build drafts; ocaml-uring diagnosed a Debian-packaging flaky test in tests/main.md.
group_summaries.activity:
- [ocaml-multicore/eio](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio): a 32-bit build fix was opened for `MSG_CMSG_CLOEXEC` overflowing OCaml's native int on 32-bit platforms, by [Thomas Leonard](https://github.com/talex5) ([ocaml-multicore/eio#917](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/917), addressing [ocaml-multicore/eio#909](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/909))
- [ocaml-multicore/eio](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio): a draft implementing `Eio.Path.native` as a backend interface with Windows support was split off from a larger patch, by [Thomas Leonard](https://github.com/talex5) ([ocaml-multicore/eio#916](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/916)), alongside the original Windows path-handling draft it was split from, now marked conflicting, by [Anil Madhavapeddy](https://github.com/avsm) ([ocaml-multicore/eio#908](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/908)); review between the two converged on treating paths lexically and possibly rejecting drive-relative paths like `C:foo`
- [ocaml-multicore/eio](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio): a draft adding device `mknod` support for creating device files beyond FIFOs was opened by [Anil Madhavapeddy](https://github.com/avsm) ([ocaml-multicore/eio#911](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/911)), prompting discussion on sharing the feature with `eio_linux`, a portable `Eio.File.Dev.t` type, and handling device numbers on platforms like Wayland where they don't fit a fixed-width field
- [ocaml-multicore/ocaml-uring](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/ocaml-uring): [Stéphane Glondu](https://github.com/glondu) opened an issue describing intermittent failures in `tests/main.md` when packaging ocaml-uring 2.15.0 for Debian, where a section of tests hangs on almost all Debian build machines though not on his own workstation, and proposed a patch tolerating read/write failures instead of asserting exact results ([ocaml-multicore/ocaml-uring#161](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/ocaml-uring/issues/161)); no PRs were opened or merged, and `main` saw no new commits since the v2.15.0 release
group_summaries.cross_repository_work: - [Stéphane Glondu](https://github.com/glondu) surfaced Debian-packaging-driven portability issues in two group repositories this week: a 32-bit build failure in [ocaml-multicore/eio](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio) ([ocaml-multicore/eio#909](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/909)) and a flaky test on Debian arm64 in [ocaml-multicore/ocaml-uring](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/ocaml-uring) ([ocaml-multicore/ocaml-uring#161](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/ocaml-uring/issues/161)), both stemming from building the ecosystem across Debian's architecture matrix
group_summaries.notable_discussions:
- On [ocaml-multicore/eio#909](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/909), whether Eio should support 32-bit at all was debated: [Thomas Leonard](https://github.com/talex5) suggested restricting `eio.unix` to 64-bit only, [Stéphane Glondu](https://github.com/glondu) noted Debian still officially supports armhf and i386, and [Anil Madhavapeddy](https://github.com/avsm) proposed following OCaml upstream's guidance of bytecode-only on 32-bit, which [ocaml-multicore/eio#917](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/917) later addressed pragmatically
- On [ocaml-multicore/eio#914](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/914), an allocation of 23 words per trace event was traced to `Runtime_events.User.write`; [Thomas Gazagnaire](https://github.com/samoht) reported the repro, [Thomas Leonard](https://github.com/talex5) pinpointed an unnecessary closure allocation in upstream `runtime_events.ml`, and [Anil Madhavapeddy](https://github.com/avsm) began benchmarking a single-buffer fix, looping in [Sadiq Jaffer](https://github.com/sadiqj)
- On [ocaml-multicore/eio#912](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/912), the need for directory `fsync` was raised to make journal-then-rename patterns durable in an embedded database; [Anil Madhavapeddy](https://github.com/avsm) agreed a path-based `sync` in `Fs.Pi.DIR` is reasonable and noted `fdatasync` may also be needed
- On [ocaml-multicore/ocaml-uring#161](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/ocaml-uring/issues/161), [Thomas Leonard](https://github.com/talex5) asked what kernel version was running on the affected CI machines, suggesting a hanging pipe read likely indicates a prior write failed rather than a kernel-specific bug, and [Stéphane Glondu](https://github.com/glondu) replied with the kernel version (6.12.96+deb13-arm64) from his debugging session
group_summaries.emerging_trends:
- Path handling is being restructured into backend-specific modules in [ocaml-multicore/eio](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio) (POSIX now, Windows next), spanning [ocaml-multicore/eio#908](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/908), [ocaml-multicore/eio#913](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/913), [ocaml-multicore/eio#915](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/915), and [ocaml-multicore/eio#916](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/916)

- __RUMINANT:core__ Nine new PRs span runtime, typing, and stdlib work: [Zane Hambly](https://github.com/Zaneham) proposed native atomic `exchange`/`compare_and_set` instructions across all five backends ([ocaml/ocaml#14980](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14980)); [Gabriel Scherer](https://github.com/gasche) opened a `Weak.Make` re-implementation reporting a 30% speedup on alt-ergo-free ([ocaml/ocaml#14979](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14979)); and [Tim McGilchrist](https://github.com/tmcgilchrist) opened two runtime-events fixes ([ocaml/ocaml#14969](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14969), [ocaml/ocaml#14966](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14966)).
- __RUMINANT:core__ Extensive design discussion continued on a **new `Hashtbl` implementation** guaranteeing deterministic iteration order by [Jeannalyse](https://github.com/Jeannalyse) ([ocaml/ocaml#14956](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14956)), feeding a broader RFC on hash-flooding protection ([ocaml/ocaml#14967](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/discussions/14967)) alongside the older randomized-seeding proposal by [Hannes Mehnert](https://github.com/hannesm) ([ocaml/ocaml#14291](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14291)); POWER-architecture support from [Tim McGilchrist](https://github.com/tmcgilchrist) neared review completion ([ocaml/ocaml#14505](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14505)).
